Different situations. 

Tkachuk and Marchenko were going to leave within 2 years for nothing by going to free agency.   

Larkin and Hellebuyck have 5 years left, so that's not a concern yet. 

Winnipeg handled it fine. They started looking into options, gauging interest and value. Goaltenders are tougher to extract value in a trade and a team has to be in a situation that makes sense. 

This was always going to be more likely when a team was mid-season and found their goaltending below expectations. Hellebuyck just had to be patient and wait a few more months while playing and raising his value. 

Hellebuyck is stuck in Winnipeg because of Hellebuyck. He's not just a good and expensive goaltender anymore, he's a red flag. 

Detroit absolutely could have handled things better. They aren't obligated to trade him, but they had a decade to construct a successful team and haven't even made the playoffs, so it shouldn't be a surprise that some players might not be satisfied with their direction. 

Larkin is doing his part professionally and taking his lumps for an unpopular choice he made to request a trade. His limited list of preferred destinations isn't doing him any favors, but he owes Hellebuyck a nod for taking some of the heat. 

Detroit is dragging its heels (speculated due to owner interference) by not allowing (or hiring) someone to even work on the problem.

You know the worst part (aside from looking ugly) is that ads on nhl uniforms are purely due to greed and profit.

Some fans online and in this sub have been endlessly mocking European teams for jersey ads and I’m not the one to defend them, they look ugly. But across Europe the teams neeed the sponsorships to survive as they finance their own hockey academies and youth programs and some of them have to pay rent for the arenas they play in. Factor in the smaller stadiums and less revenue from tickets and broadcasting rights and jersey ads are a matter of necessity for the teams

But in NHL I feel like there was zero reason to keep ads on jerseys and helmets. And yet they did it. We can only wish we won’t get a second jersey ad anytime soon
